articles.title: Linq Raises $90 Million in New Funding Led by Andreessen Horowitz to Build the Infrastructure Platform for AI Agents
articles.snippet: Linq Raises $90 Million in New Funding Led by Andreessen Horowitz to Build the Infrastructure Platform for AI Agents PR Newswire
articles.text:
Linq Raises $90 Million in New Funding Led by Andreessen Horowitz to Build the Infrastructure Platform for AI Agents
News provided by
Linq
Nov 18, 2026, 22:45 ET
Share this article
Share this article
Every business and every person will have an agent. With more than 1 billion messages processed, Linq is building the infrastructure to put them to work.
SAN FRANCISCO , Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Linq , the infrastructure platform for AI agents, today announced $90 million in new funding led by Andreessen Horowitz, with continued participation from TQ Ventures, Mucker Capital, and Abstract, and new participation from Anthos and Left Lane Capital. Ben Horowitz will join its board of directors.
Continue Reading
Linq’s Co-Founders: Patrick Sullivan (CTO), Elliott Potter (CEO), and Jared Mattsson (President)
The internet gave every business a website. The iPhone gave every business an app. Now AI is giving every business, and every person, an agent. Cloudflare reports that more than half of internet traffic is no longer human, with AI agent requests on its network up more than 1,700% in a year. These are not simple, customer-service chatbots: these agents book, buy, and make plans by communicating with people and using software on their behalf.
Messaging was Linq's first product and remains a core part of its growing AI infrastructure platform. As the provider for DoorDash, Town, Tomo, and hundreds of others, Linq has already processed more than 1 billion messages. DoorDash uses Linq to help customers find food, build a cart, and check out in a single thread. And now, as an Apple Messaging Service Provider, Linq can help more enterprises launch and scale customer-facing agents on the same channel.
"The best AI experiences fit naturally into people's lives," said Aryan Shah, Head of AI research at DoorDash. "Linq gives us the messaging infrastructure to bring ordering into a familiar conversation, so customers can go from deciding what they want to placing an order in one thread."
"Agents will communicate and get work done just like people do. Linq gives agents the infrastructure to do both at scale," said Ben Horowitz, cofounder and general partner at Andreessen Horowitz.
Messaging is the beginning of a larger shift: people will describe what they need, and agents will get it done. Linq's computer use offering gives agents access to physical computing infrastructure to interact with software and complete tasks. HD Calling for Agents adds voice calling to the platform. The funding will support continued investment in messaging and the expansion of Linq's product lineup through its own software, hardware infrastructure, and strategic partnerships.
"Clicking through five screens to make a payment will become two words to an agent: 'pay rent,'" said Elliott Potter, CEO of Linq. "We help developers build customer-facing agents that use human tools to do human work."
Companies can learn more at https://linqapp.com/
About Linq
Linq is the platform for building AI agents. It brings together messaging and an expanding set of tools for interacting with the world, helping developers spend less time assembling infrastructure and more time building products. Learn more at https://linqapp.com/
Riley Munks
PR Advisor

Pulley Raises $64 Million to Expand AI-Powered Real Estate Development Platform
November 19, 2026
Pulley , a technology company providing AI-powered permitting and development services, has raised $64 million in funding to expand its platform and introduce new products designed to accelerate commercial real estate development.
The financing includes a $41 million Series B round led by Jump Capital , with participation from Catalyst Investors , and a $23 million Series A round led by CRV and Susa Ventures. The announcement follows fivefold year-over-year growth in Pulley’s annual recurring revenue.
The company plans to use the capital to expand its permitting operations and develop tools that help businesses evaluate potential development sites, navigate regulatory requirements and identify construction design issues before submitting projects for approval.
Pulley provides permitting services to major retailers, restaurants, financial institutions, manufacturers and data center operators. Its customers include Amazon, Starbucks, JLL, Meta and Equinix.
The company combines artificial intelligence, regulatory data and a nationwide team of more than 75 licensed professionals to help customers manage construction approvals across all 50 states.
According to Pulley, its platform has supported more than $21 billion in commercial construction projects and helped customers save a combined 11,750 weeks of project development time.
“The speed at which we build is one of the most important challenges facing America over the next decade,” said Charlie Jacobson , co-founder and CEO of Pulley. “To remain a global leader in AI, bring manufacturing back home, reach energy independence and sustain job growth, we need to build orders of magnitude faster. The single biggest lever to building faster is to get started faster.”
Pulley’s existing services include regulatory due diligence, permitting strategy development, construction plan reviews and coordination with local government agencies.
The company also participates in private plan review programs covering more than 2,000 cities and counties, allowing its certified professionals to approve building plans in jurisdictions that authorize private review.
Pulley said its customers typically receive one round of jurisdictional review comments per project, while more than 40% of projects receive approval without any comments. The company also reported a 65% reduction in review comments in 2026 compared with 2025.
“Pulley’s understanding of jurisdictional requirements and code interpretations helps us anticipate issues before design is complete,” said Karen Rojas , design, development and delivery manager at Meta. “As we move toward a single partner managing permitting from site development through construction, Pulley is helping shape our approach.”
The new funding will support Pulley’s expansion beyond permitting into earlier stages of real estate development.
Planned capabilities include site selection tools that combine zoning and permitting regulations with information about utility availability, local community sentiment and other development constraints.
Pulley is also introducing AI-powered construction drawing reviews intended to identify building code compliance issues during the design process, reducing the need for revisions after plans are submitted to regulatory authorities.

articles.title: GlassPoint Raises $24 Million to Support Middle East Expansion
articles.snippet: GlassPoint Raises $24 Million to Support Middle East Expansion Mercom Capital Group
articles.text:
November 19, 2026
Staff
Solar
From: Mercom India
GlassPoint , a company that provides solar thermal-based energy solutions, has raised $24 million in a funding round led by European asset management firm New Investment Solutions, with participation from new investor MITO Tech Ventures.
The latest investment takes GlassPoint’s total funding raised in 2026 to $44 million. The company raised $20 million in January of this year in a round also led by New Investment Solutions, with participation from returning investor MIG Capital.
GlassPoint said the funding will support its expansion across the Middle East, including establishing operations in Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, and Oman and expanding its presence in the United Arab Emirates.
The expansion will include executive, engineering, and operational hiring and additional local project delivery capacity. GlassPoint relocated its executive team from the U.S. and Europe to the UAE earlier this year.
“The Middle East is building one of the world’s most ambitious industrial economies, and that growth will require extraordinary amounts of reliable, competitively priced heat,” said Rod MacGregor, CEO of GlassPoint. “Recent events have reinforced the importance of energy security, and our platform addresses both the economic and strategic needs of heavy industry.
The company’s industrial heat platform combines concentrated solar thermal technology with thermal energy storage and can incorporate multiple energy sources. GlassPoint said the system is designed to provide continuous process heat for industrial operations.
Its enclosed trough technology converts solar energy directly into heat. The technology is paired with GlassPoint’s Unify thermal storage system, which stores thermal energy to support heat delivery during periods without sunlight.
GlassPoint has deployed its technology in Oman through the Miraah project, which has delivered up to 2,000 tons of solar steam per day for almost a decade, according to the company.
In Saudi Arabia, GlassPoint is developing the Ma’aden Solar I project at Ras Al Khair. The project is designed to provide 500 MW of continuous thermal output to Ma’aden’s alumina refining operations using a 1.5 GW solar array.
Global VC funding for the solar sector in the first nine months of 2026 came to $2 billion in 60 deals, a 31% decrease YoY compared to $2.9 billion raised in 55 deals in 9M 2025, according to Mercom’s 9M and Q3 2026 Solar Funding and M&A report. A total of 192 VC investors have participated in solar funding in 9M 2026.

Protecting where software gets built: StepSecurity’s $20 million Series A
Today, we’re announcing an oversubscribed $20 million Series A led by Elephant to expand protection for developer machines, package downloads, CI/CD pipelines, and agent sandboxes.
Varun Sharma
View LinkedIn
November 18, 2026
Share on X
Share on X
Share on LinkedIn

Follow our RSS feed

Ashish and I still remember the incident-response war rooms after the SolarWinds supply chain attack in Dec 2020. Ashish was at Uber and I was at Microsoft. We were trying to answer two questions: were we affected and how would we prevent an attack like this from happening again? The cybersecurity solutions we had relied on offered frustratingly little help with the questions in front of us. Our teams scrambled to piece together the answers and build homegrown workarounds under high pressure.
A few months later, attackers inserted malicious code into Codecov’s Bash Uploader, bringing the same scramble back. The malicious code stole secrets from customers’ CI/CD environments for roughly two months before it was discovered.
The security tools we relied on focused on vulnerabilities attackers might exploit in production. These attacks exposed a different risk. Malicious code could cause damage on a developer’s machine or in a CI/CD pipeline. It did not need to reach production.
Those experiences drove us to start StepSecurity in 2021. We wanted security teams to have visibility and protection in the environments where software gets built.
We raised our seed round of $3 million in May 2024. Since then, our ARR grew 5× in 2024 and again in 2025. In 2026, we have already crossed that 5× growth milestone and are on pace for our biggest growth year yet.
More than 20,000 open-source projects now use our Harden-Runner community tier. Enterprise customers including Circle, Dexcom, Kong, Mercor, Mercari, Chainguard, and XBOW trust StepSecurity to protect their software supply chains.
Today, we’re announcing an oversubscribed $20 million Series A led by Elephant, with participation from existing investors Runtime Ventures, Inner Loop Capital, and SaaS Ventures.
The problem that led us to start StepSecurity has grown more urgent and now extends to every knowledge worker. Any knowledge worker can ask an AI agent to perform a task, such as creating a spreadsheet. To complete it, the agent may download open-source packages and execute code.
Software is now built everywhere: by agents on laptops, in the cloud, and inside pipelines. That creates a larger attack surface, even as AI makes attacks easier to launch.
Recent attacks show how developer tools and workstations can expose sensitive systems. Examples include the tampered Claude Code extension in Cursor’s marketplace and Binance’s reported breach.
This funding will strengthen the protection our products provide for developer machines, package downloads, and CI/CD. It will also help us build protection for agent sandboxes.
